message_1_subject: Redwood demo follow-up: stakeholder map & next steps
message_1_body:
Hi Samantha / Rajiv,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciated the thoughtful questions from your security and infra teams. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Highlights from the demo: deterministic latency with Dedicated pools, prefix caching to reduce token cost, and our rollout tools for canarying new model versions.
- Action items I captured:
  1) EnterpriseCorp to share a stakeholder map (economic buyer, security/compliance owners, legal/procurement contact).
  2) We to provide the SOC 2 summary, sample DPA, and a draft quote tied to the usage profile you shared.
  3) Schedule a short follow-up with your security lead to walk through evidence paths (30 min).

Attached is a quick Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that we can iterate on — please drop in names for owners and estimated procurement timelines.

If it helps, we can also start a procurement exception request for the SLA/discount items you called out so your procurement team has a single doc to review. 

Best,
Marissa

message_3_subject: FWD: EnterpriseCorp procurement path — need approvals for exceptions
message_3_body:
Team — forwarding EnterpriseCorp's reply. Quick ask: 

1) Can we pre-approve a procurement exception path? They asked for the vendor intake to be accelerated. Specific asks we should anticipate: 10% partner discount on the first year, and a partial SLA exception (99.9% instead of our standard 99.95%) for the Dedicated deployment due to their on-prem constraints.
2) Legal: can you pre-review the DPA and confirm any redlines we should expect?
3) Eng/SE: can you assemble the SOC 2 evidence pack (high-level summary + where docs live)? Aditya, can you confirm if the architecture notes in the MAP are sufficient for Rajiv or do we need a deeper runbook?

HubSpot deal: EPC-2026-0421 (link below). I'll prepare a procurement-exception request doc to share with Procurement once we have internal approvals. Ideally we'd have approvals by end of week so Samantha can keep momentum.

Thanks,
Marissa

message_5_subject: Re: procurement exception approvals — EnterpriseCorp EPC-2026-0421
message_5_body:
Marissa — reviewed. Summary: 

- Legal can provisionally approve a limited DPA variation for EnterpriseCorp subject to our standard data processing safeguards and a 30-day review clause.
- Finance/legal can approve a one-time 10% discount for year one, conditioned on Procurement signing the intake form and agreeing in writing to the exception.
- SLA variance to 99.9% is acceptable as a documented exception for this customer; please note we will include a clause that any extended outage credits require escalation to product/legal.

Actionable: Neha will prepare a short internal memo (1 page) documenting the exception rationale and conditions. Once that's ready, Marissa please attach it to the procurement-exception packet you send to their Procurement contact.

-Neha
